## Building End-to-End Support in Europe: Paris GSCC Nears Completion of Its Next Phase


When we opened our[Global Supply Chain Center (GSCC)](https://www.cryoport.com/news-blog-cryoport-systems-redefines-the-global-supply-chain-with-launch-of-new-facility-near-paris-france/) in Louvres, France, just minutes from Paris Charles de Gaulle Airport, we spoke about a vision that extended beyond logistics. The 57,000-square-foot campus was designed to be a strategic hub for the life sciences industry, bringing together temperature-controlled supply chain solutions and creating a foundation for expanded services to support advanced therapies from development through to commercialization. As part of that vision, we shared plans to add our comprehensive BioServices in the months following the facility’s opening, including biostorage, custom kit production, packaging, labeling, and Qualified Person (QP) services. While our comprehensive logistics capabilities remain fully operational and available in Paris, we’re excited to share that the next phase of our GSCC is nearing completion.


What started as an ambitious vision has steadily taken shape over the course of the year through construction, qualification, validation, and countless hours of teamwork across multiple functions. Today, the BioServices phase is transitioning from building and preparation to the final stages of operational readiness, putting us on track for a targeted go-live in first quarter 2027.


##### Progress Across Key Workstreams


Over the past several months, countless teams across the globe have worked side by side to move the project forward. Construction activities have been completed, and the focus has shifted toward the critical milestones that will enable the facility to begin serving customers with end-to-end supply chain capabilities.


Several of those milestones are now within reach. Equipment qualification and process mapping activities are in the final stretch, providing confidence that systems, workflows, and procedures will perform as intended. Validation of the Environmental Monitoring System (EMS) is also progressing as planned, while regulatory authorization activities with MIA/ANSM continue to advance toward approval by the end of November.


Preparations are also currently underway for Process Qualification (PQ), one of the final major steps before launch. Teams are completing the extensive documentation needed to support operations, including SOPs, work instructions, qualification reports, training records, and system documentation. Much of this work will culminate in December as processes and documentation are finalized, setting the stage for a smooth transition into routine operations.


##### Entering the Home Stretch


Over the next several weeks, a series of important milestones will arrive in quick succession. November brings completion of key qualification activities, EMS validation, and regulatory approval. In December, we will focus on Process Qualification execution and final operational readiness activities. By mid-December, the core qualification work is expected to be complete, allowing the team to zero in on the final preparations leading into January’s launch.


The closer we get to kicking off, the clearer the impact of this project becomes. The BioServices expansion will position our capabilities in one of Europe’s key advanced therapies markets and strengthen our ability to support customers with high-quality, locally accessible biostorage, kit production, packaging, labeling and QP services. It also represents a significant investment in future growth in EMEA and fulfills our endeavor to provide global reach via a local presence.


##### A Team Effort Driving Success


Of course, projects of this scale are never the work of one team alone. Every milestone reached so far reflects the efforts of colleagues across disciplines and geographies at Cryoport Systems. From engineers and validation specialists to quality professionals, project and program managers, regulatory experts, and operational teams, each group has played a role in turning plans into reality. The collaboration demonstrated throughout the project has been a key driver of its success.


A year ago, the launch of BioServices at our Paris facility was a future goal marked on a timeline. Today, it is just weeks away. As we continue through the final qualification and approval activities, we look forward to sharing more updates and soon, celebrating the opening of the next phase of our Global Supply Chain Center that will help shape a new chapter of BioServices in Europe.
